hero.title: Welcome to Vix, the IDE that already knows your keys.
hero.tagline: Save with <k>Ctrl+S</k>, find with <k>Ctrl+F</k> and reach everything else from a menu bar or the <k>Ctrl+P</k> command palette. Language servers, a debugger, Git, Org mode and a database workbench are built in, in your terminal or a native window, so Vix is useful the moment it opens.
hero.installNote: Or use the installer script, PowerShell, npm, or cargo install vix-tui — see all install options. The command is vix.
who.title: Made for the way you already work
who.1.heading: You live in the terminal but miss your IDE
who.1.text: Go to definition, rename, a debugger and a Git panel, over SSH or in tmux, without a config project.
who.2.heading: You tried Vim or Helix and bounced off modes
who.2.text: Vix starts with the shortcuts every other app uses. Switch on the Vi keymap when you want it.
who.3.heading: You came to Emacs for Org mode
who.3.text: Agenda, tables with formulas, Column View, Org-roam and dailies are built in, with menus to find them.
who.4.heading: You work with data and APIs
who.4.text: Query a database, send an HTTP request, inspect a container and edit the CSV it produced, in one window.
from.title: Read the guide for where you're coming from
faq.title: Frequently asked
faq.1.q: Do I have to learn modal editing?
faq.1.a: No. The default keymap uses the same shortcuts as your other apps. Vi and Spacemacs keymaps are one menu choice away if you want them.
faq.2.q: Do I need plugins to get started?
faq.2.a: No. Everything on this page ships in the one <c>vix</c> binary. Rhai scripts are there for adding your own commands, not for filling gaps.
faq.3.q: Does it work over SSH and in tmux?
faq.3.a: Yes. Vix is a terminal program, so run it on the remote machine as you would any other. Since 2.0, Vix also opens a folder on another machine from your local Vix over SSH (<c>vix ssh://host/path</c>, or File → Open Remote…). That is experimental.
faq.4.a: Pick whichever of five licenses suits you: Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, MIT, GPL-2.0 or GPL-3.0. For locked-down machines, the minimal build makes no network connections and starts no other program.
open.title: Free, and built in the open
open.text: Vix's source is licensed under your choice of Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, MIT, GPL-2.0 or GPL-3.0. Development is specification-driven: each of its crates has a spec that the code implements. How the project uses AI assistance is set out in its AI statement.
cta.title: Try Vix in thirty seconds
cta.note: Then run <c>vix</c> in any folder. Press <k>F1</k> for every shortcut.
